entry.title: Did I just spent 6 months building a product that no one wants (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: For the past few months, I've been building a product "Linden". Its a low latency deterministic layer for ai agents. Linden helps businesses verify AI-generated outputs before they lead to real-world actions. It evaluates AI outputs against expected schemas, trusted data, and business rules to determine whether an action should be allowed, flagged, regenerated, blocked, or sent for human review. Linden helps businesses ensure their AI agents don't just produce convincing answers - they make decisions that align with actual business requirements, verified information, and configured limits. I have tried cold email outreach that didn't work. Published a professional demo across multiple platforms, drove 0 signups. Now, i don't know if I just built something that serves no purpose. However, when i was building this, i did a research, looked at a lot of articles talking about the same thing. If this problem exists, then why no one willing to try it out? Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50189266 Points: 3 # Comments: 0

entry.title: Show HN: I built a Markdown and raw HTML blog platform scoring 99 on PageSpeed (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: Hello. I built a blogging platform on my own over two years. I like running my blog, but I couldn't find a blogging platform I really liked. First. I thought a blog had to be really lightweight. Fortunately, after a lot of effort, I was able to achieve satisfactory results. (99 to 100 score) Here is a sample blog: https://bloffy.bloffy.blog/en You can check it with PageSpeed Insights: https://pagespeed.web.dev/analysis?url=https://bloffy.bloffy... SEO score of the sample blog is low because I blocked it from search engine indexing (noindex). Second. I think bloggers should have control over their own blog. The blogging platforms I used had several problems. Unnecessary JavaScript chunks. Ads that the platform inserted into my blog, not my own ads. Cannot manage multiple blogs. An editor that makes it hard to write semantic markup. Limited customization options. I was dissatisfied with the difficulty of placing my own ads. And to solve this, I spent quite a long time researching and developing it on my own, and finally created it. I'm glad to share this launch with HN. I would appreciate any criticism, feedback, and interest. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50189175 Points: 2 # Comments: 0
